The function then returns `\"Kaipu Record — \"`, which ends in a space: the same trailing space the doc comment says Windows refuses. Tests in `workspace-name.test.ts` check the folder name never ends in a space. `?` and `*` still map to the same folder; `create` then refuses the second as \"exists\" and the dialog says so, which I think is the right outcome."

content.text: Checked the code paths and the earlier threads. Now writing up the review.

findings.title: Picking the folder the workspace already points at still toasts "now points to the new folder"
findings.body: `relocateWorkspace` now returns early with the unchanged entry when the chosen path is the current one (`relocate.ts:43`). The result is still `{ ok: true }`, so `onRelocated` here and the dialog's `onRelocated(result)` (`workspace-dialog.tsx:145`) show `folderChanged`: "Done. {name} now points to the new folder." The picker opens at `dirname(entry.path)`, so picking the same folder is easy, and the user is told something changed when nothing did. Consider distinguishing the no-op, or wording the toast so it is true in both cases.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade is kept in its own `pendingColorUpgrade` marker and applied when the folder returns
contracts.equivalent_path: The `pendingIdentity` branch in `availability` (registry.ts:663), which writes the cached name, color and initials over the folder's file.
contracts.before_after: Before, the upgrade set `pendingIdentity`, so when the folder came back the cache overwrote the folder's identity.json, even if another Mac had renamed or recolored it. Now `availability` re-reads identity.json and writes only if it still holds the old Default and rose (`isOldDefault`, registry.ts:202). Otherwise the folder wins: the `stale` branch (registry.ts:694-707) adopts it and clears the marker. `edit` clears the marker (registry.ts:629) and sets `pendingIdentity`, so an explicit edit still wins. Probes that write the file (registry.ts:736-741) and `edit`'s no-change early return (registry.ts:585) also account for the new marker.
contracts.visible_effect: A Default workspace renamed or recolored on another Mac while this folder was away keeps that name and color. Otherwise the folder gets the Kaipu color on reconnect. The new tests cover renamed, recolored and edit-wins.
contracts.failure_mode: The write is a read-compare-write on the target: `readIdentity` (registry.ts:657) then `writeIdentity` (registry.ts:684) with no await in between, so the window is narrow. `availability` is not under the registry's update lock, so a concurrent `edit` could in theory land its atomic write in that gap and be overwritten for one probe. `pendingIdentity` has the same shape. If the write fails, the marker stays and the next probe retries. In read-only sessions (corrupt-prefs fallback) no marker exists.

contracts.action: "Change folder…" on the folder it already points at returns early, before the switch transaction
contracts.equivalent_path: `relocateActive` (switch-transaction) for the active workspace, and `registry.relocate` for the others.
contracts.before_after: `checkRelocate` still runs first, so a refused folder is refused as before. If the path is unchanged, the new code returns `{ ok: true, entry }` without asking windows to prepare, dropping captures or bumping the generation. The caller `relocateFolder` (index.ts:340-342) still runs `reg.availability`, which rewrites a hand-deleted identity file.
contracts.visible_effect: No Save/Discard prompt and no route remount for a no-op. The success toast still says the folder changed (see the finding).
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. The `current` guard cannot be undefined after a passing `checkRelocate`.

contracts.action: `checkRelocate` accepts a folder with `.kaipu` items and no identity.json when the entry is `pendingInit`
contracts.equivalent_path: `availability`, which writes the registered id's identity into a reachable folder that has none (registry.ts:724-747).
contracts.before_after: The same rule is applied for the entry's `pendingInit` state in both `checkRelocate` and `relocate` (which calls it). After the move the probe writes identity.json under the registered id and clears `pendingInit`. A non-pending entry still gets `has-items-no-identity`. A folder holding another workspace's identity is still refused as `different` (registry.ts:836-838), although `availability` would adopt that id for a `pendingInit` entry (registry.ts:711-721); the earlier thread (4439290166) raised that second case.
contracts.visible_effect: A Default registered while its drive was unplugged can be pointed at the remounted folder.
contracts.failure_mode: A refusal shows the existing message. `relocate` write failures return `not-writable`.

contracts.action: A rejected create, edit or relocate IPC call now shows an "outcome unknown" message instead of nothing
contracts.equivalent_path: The refusal path (`setRefusal(result.reason)` / `setFolderError(...)`), and `changeFolder` in the context (workspaces-context.tsx:172-191).
contracts.before_after: Before, a rejection went unhandled: `finally` freed the button and nothing was shown. Now `catch` sets `create-uncertain` / `edit-uncertain` or `relocateUncertain`, and the context shows a toast. The wording does not claim failure, since main may already have applied the change. The new strings exist in en and es.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees an alert (or a toast) asking them to check the list or folder before retrying. The busy/relocating flag is reset in `finally`.
contracts.failure_mode: The `catch` also covers synchronous throws from `onSaved` / `onCreated`, which would show the "uncertain" text after a successful call. In practice the dialog is closing then. `checkLocation(...).then` (workspace-dialog.tsx:95) still has no `.catch`, but it is not part of this diff.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed. The rollback in `edit` removes the identity file it just wrote when the folder had none (registry.ts:636-640).
Confirmed. `edit` re-checks the name inside the locked `update` and throws `NameTakenError` (registry.ts:621), and the catch undoes the folder write.
Confirmed. `refusalMessage` uses `editNotWritable` and `editFailed` when editing (workspace-dialog.tsx:353-360).
Confirmed. The late answer now resolves inside `await act(async …)` (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:164).

The main case is fixed: a `pendingInit` entry now accepts a folder with `.kaipu` items and no identity (registry.ts:848), with a test. The second case from the thread is not: a `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder holds another id is still refused as `different` (registry.ts:836-838), while `availability` adopts that id (registry.ts:711-721). Fix it or say it is intentional.

`switch-transaction.ts` is not in this change. `relocateActive` still calls `dropPendingCaptures`, so a pending screenshot toast is still dismissed when the active workspace is relocated. Please decide whether to keep that.

Fixed. `relocateWorkspace` returns early when the chosen path equals the current one (relocate.ts:42-43), before any window is asked to prepare. The new test checks that no window is asked, that nothing is dropped, and that the generation stays at 1. The toast still says the folder changed (see my new comment).
Fixed. The "Move to" sentence is gone from both locales (en.json:2623, es.json:2623), and the test now asserts its absence (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:294).

Fixed. The dialog catches a rejection and shows `relocateUncertain` (workspace-dialog.tsx:147-149), and the context shows a toast (workspaces-context.tsx:177-181). The text avoids claiming failure, which is right because main may already have applied the change.
Fixed. The test now resolves a relocate, checks that Save stays disabled, then picks another color and checks that Save becomes enabled (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:343-355).

input.summary: The change closes most of the earlier threads. The deferred color upgrade now has its own marker. It writes only if the folder still holds the old Default and rose, otherwise the folder wins, and an explicit edit clears it. `pendingInit` workspaces can be relocated. A same-folder pick returns early. Rejected create, edit and relocate calls show an "outcome unknown" message. I found one small issue: picking the folder a workspace already points at still toasts "now points to the new folder". Two earlier threads stay open: `pendingInit` relocation to a folder holding another workspace's id is still refused as `different`, and the capture drop on relocating the active workspace is untouched.

findings.title: Picking the folder the workspace already points at still toasts "now points to the new folder"
findings.body: `relocateWorkspace` now returns early with the unchanged entry when the chosen path is the current one (`relocate.ts:43`). The result is still `{ ok: true }`, so `onRelocated` here and the dialog's `onRelocated(result)` (`workspace-dialog.tsx:145`) show `folderChanged`: "Done. {name} now points to the new folder." The picker opens at `dirname(entry.path)`, so picking the same folder is easy, and the user is told something changed when nothing did. Consider distinguishing the no-op, or wording the toast so it is true in both cases.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade is kept in its own `pendingColorUpgrade` marker and applied when the folder returns
contracts.equivalent_path: The `pendingIdentity` branch in `availability` (registry.ts:663), which writes the cached name, color and initials over the folder's file.
contracts.before_after: Before, the upgrade set `pendingIdentity`, so when the folder came back the cache overwrote the folder's identity.json, even if another Mac had renamed or recolored it. Now `availability` re-reads identity.json and writes only if it still holds the old Default and rose (`isOldDefault`, registry.ts:202). Otherwise the folder wins: the `stale` branch (registry.ts:694-707) adopts it and clears the marker. `edit` clears the marker (registry.ts:629) and sets `pendingIdentity`, so an explicit edit still wins. Probes that write the file (registry.ts:736-741) and `edit`'s no-change early return (registry.ts:585) also account for the new marker.
contracts.visible_effect: A Default workspace renamed or recolored on another Mac while this folder was away keeps that name and color. Otherwise the folder gets the Kaipu color on reconnect. The new tests cover renamed, recolored and edit-wins.
contracts.failure_mode: The write is a read-compare-write on the target: `readIdentity` (registry.ts:657) then `writeIdentity` (registry.ts:684) with no await in between, so the window is narrow. `availability` is not under the registry's update lock, so a concurrent `edit` could in theory land its atomic write in that gap and be overwritten for one probe. `pendingIdentity` has the same shape. If the write fails, the marker stays and the next probe retries. In read-only sessions (corrupt-prefs fallback) no marker exists.

contracts.action: "Change folder…" on the folder it already points at returns early, before the switch transaction
contracts.equivalent_path: `relocateActive` (switch-transaction) for the active workspace, and `registry.relocate` for the others.
contracts.before_after: `checkRelocate` still runs first, so a refused folder is refused as before. If the path is unchanged, the new code returns `{ ok: true, entry }` without asking windows to prepare, dropping captures or bumping the generation. The caller `relocateFolder` (index.ts:340-342) still runs `reg.availability`, which rewrites a hand-deleted identity file.
contracts.visible_effect: No Save/Discard prompt and no route remount for a no-op. The success toast still says the folder changed (see the finding).
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. The `current` guard cannot be undefined after a passing `checkRelocate`.

contracts.action: `checkRelocate` accepts a folder with `.kaipu` items and no identity.json when the entry is `pendingInit`
contracts.equivalent_path: `availability`, which writes the registered id's identity into a reachable folder that has none (registry.ts:724-747).
contracts.before_after: The same rule is applied for the entry's `pendingInit` state in both `checkRelocate` and `relocate` (which calls it). After the move the probe writes identity.json under the registered id and clears `pendingInit`. A non-pending entry still gets `has-items-no-identity`. A folder holding another workspace's identity is still refused as `different` (registry.ts:836-838), although `availability` would adopt that id for a `pendingInit` entry (registry.ts:711-721); the earlier thread (4439290166) raised that second case.
contracts.visible_effect: A Default registered while its drive was unplugged can be pointed at the remounted folder.
contracts.failure_mode: A refusal shows the existing message. `relocate` write failures return `not-writable`.

contracts.action: A rejected create, edit or relocate IPC call now shows an "outcome unknown" message instead of nothing
